title: Unit 5: Human Health, Nutrition, and Disease
description: Comprehensive questions covering Grade 9 Biology Unit 5

questions.question: What is food?
options: Any substance that is harmful to the body
Any beneficial substance eaten, drunk, or taken into the body to sustain life, provide energy, promote growth, etc.
Only substances that come from animals
Any liquid consumed by an organism
questions.correctAnswer: Any beneficial substance eaten, drunk, or taken into the body to sustain life, provide energy, promote growth, etc.
questions.explanation: Food is any beneficial substance that is eaten, drunk, or otherwise taken into the body to sustain life, provide energy, promote growth, etc. Food is usually of plant, animal, or fungal origin and contains essential nutrients.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an importance of food in living things?
questions.explanation: The importance of food includes growth, providing energy, replacement of damaged tissues, and protection from diseases. Increasing body temperature beyond normal is not a function of food.

questions.question: What is nutrition?
options: The process of taking in food and converting it into energy and other vital nutrients required for life
The process of eliminating waste from the body
questions.correctAnswer: The process of taking in food and converting it into energy and other vital nutrients required for life
questions.explanation: Nutrition is the process of taking in food and converting it into energy and other vital nutrients required for life. Energy obtained from food is important for different activities of the body.

questions.question: What are nutrients?
options: Important chemical substances that are found in foods
questions.correctAnswer: Important chemical substances that are found in foods
questions.explanation: Nutrients are important chemical substances that are found in foods. The five important classes of nutrients are carbohydrates, proteins, lipids (fats and oil), vitamins, minerals and water.

questions.question: Which nutrients are called macronutrients?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrate, protein and fats are required in large quantities and are called macronutrients. Minerals and vitamins are needed in very small quantities and are called micronutrients.

questions.question: Which nutrients are called micronutrients?
questions.explanation: Minerals and vitamins are needed in very small quantities and are called micronutrients. They do not supply energy but play an important role in the regulation of metabolic activity.

questions.question: What are the three elements that carbohydrates are composed of?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are composed of three elements: carbon, oxygen and hydrogen. The human body gets carbohydrates from green plants.

questions.question: How much energy does one gram of carbohydrate provide on average?
questions.explanation: One gram of carbohydrate can provide, on average, 16 kilojoules (kJ) of energy.

questions.question: What is the molecular formula of glucose?
questions.explanation: Glucose is a monosaccharide with the molecular formula $C_6H_{12}O_6$. It is also known as a hexose sugar because it has six carbon atoms.

questions.question: What is the general chemical formula of disaccharides?
questions.explanation: The general chemical formula of disaccharides is $C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}$. Examples include maltose (glucose + glucose), sucrose (glucose + fructose), and lactose (glucose + galactose).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a monosaccharide?
questions.explanation: Glucose, fructose, and galactose are monosaccharides (simple sugars). Sucrose is a disaccharide composed of glucose and fructose.

questions.question: What is the main function of carbohydrates in the human body?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are types of nutrients that provide energy for the human body. They are the major sources of energy in our diet.

questions.question: Which nutrient provides dietary fiber?
questions.explanation: An unavailable or indigestible carbohydrate provides dietary fiber. Fiber does not serve as a source of energy but helps prevent constipation and keeps the colon healthy.

questions.question: What is the function of dietary fiber in the body?
options: Helps prevent constipation and keeps the colon healthy
questions.correctAnswer: Helps prevent constipation and keeps the colon healthy
questions.explanation: Fiber adds bulk to the contents of the colon, softens feces, and reduces the time needed for undigested residues to pass out of the body. This helps prevent constipation and keeps the colon healthy.

questions.question: How much energy does one gram of lipid provide?
questions.explanation: One gram of lipid gives 37 kJ of energy. Fats and oils are high-energy nutrients that provide 35 to 45% of caloric intake.

questions.question: What is the difference between fats and oils?
options: Fats are from plants, oils are from animals
Fats are solid at room temperature while oils are liquid at room temperature
Fats provide more energy than oils
questions.correctAnswer: Fats are solid at room temperature while oils are liquid at room temperature
questions.explanation: Fats are obtained from animal sources and are solid at room temperature, while oils are from plant sources and are liquid at room temperature.

questions.question: Which fat-soluble vitamins require dietary fat for absorption?
options: Vitamin A, D, E and K
questions.correctAnswer: Vitamin A, D, E and K
questions.explanation: Dietary fat serves as a vehicle for the absorption of the fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K.

questions.question: What elements make up proteins?
questions.explanation: Proteins are made up of amino acids composed of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen.

questions.question: How much energy does one gram of protein provide?
questions.explanation: One gram of protein can provide 17 kJ of energy. Proteins are primarily used for growth of the body and building new cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major function of proteins in the body?
questions.explanation: Proteins are nutrients which provide growth of the body, build new cells, and repair damaged tissues. They also form enzymes, some hormones, and cell membranes.

questions.question: Which mineral is used to synthesize hemoglobin in red blood cells?
questions.explanation: Iron is a mineral which synthesizes the hemoglobin of red blood cells. Hemoglobin is a molecule which carries oxygen in blood.

questions.question: Which mineral is needed for proper functioning of the thyroid gland?
questions.explanation: Iodine is a mineral which makes the thyroid gland work properly. The source of iodine is iodized salt and seafood.

questions.question: Which mineral is used to build teeth and bones and helps muscles to contract?
questions.explanation: Calcium is used to build teeth and bones, makes muscles contract, and helps in the transmission of nerve impulses. Important sources of calcium are milk and cheese.

questions.question: Which vitamin deficiency causes scurvy?
questions.explanation: Scurvy is a deficiency disease caused by a lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid). It causes bleeding under the skin, bleeding gums, and poor healing of wounds.

questions.question: Which vitamin deficiency causes rickets?
questions.explanation: Rickets is a deficiency disease caused by the shortage of vitamin D. It results in deformed bones in the legs of children.

questions.question: Which disease is caused by vitamin B1 (thiamine) deficiency?
questions.explanation: Beriberi is caused by deficiency of thiamine (vitamin B1). It affects the nervous system and cardiovascular system.

questions.question: Which vitamin deficiency causes night blindness?
questions.explanation: Night blindness is caused by deficiency of vitamin A. Vitamin A is important for vision, especially in low light conditions.

questions.question: What is the deficiency disease caused by lack of iron?
questions.explanation: Anemia is a deficiency disease caused by the lack of iron. Insufficient iron leads to less haemoglobin production, resulting in less oxygen transportation, causing weakness and tiredness.

questions.question: What is the deficiency disease caused by lack of iodine?
questions.explanation: Goiter is caused by iodine deficiency. Iodine is needed for proper thyroid gland function; without enough iodine, the thyroid gland enlarges.

questions.question: What is kwashiorkor caused by?
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor is a deficiency disease caused by inadequate protein content in the human body, especially in children. Symptoms include dry or flaky skin, swelling of leg and abdomen, and hair color changes.

questions.question: What is marasmus caused by?
questions.explanation: Marasmus is a deficiency disease caused by inadequate carbohydrate content in the human body. Symptoms include thin arms and legs, little muscle, and an old-looking face.

questions.question: What is a balanced diet?
options: A diet that contains only proteins and vitamins
A diet that contains all nutrients in the correct amount and proportion
A diet that contains only carbohydrates and fats
A diet that avoids all fats
questions.correctAnswer: A diet that contains all nutrients in the correct amount and proportion
questions.explanation: A balanced diet is the diet that contains all of the nutrients in the correct amount and proportion. It must contain enough carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, mineral salts, plant fiber, and water.

questions.question: Which group of people needs relatively more energy food than women?
questions.explanation: Men should eat relatively more energy food than women because women have a higher fat content with lower metabolic rate, while men have more muscular tissue with higher metabolic rate.

questions.question: What is malnutrition?
options: Eating only one type of food
Insufficient, excessive or imbalanced consumption of nutrients leading to health problems
Eating food from only plant sources
questions.correctAnswer: Insufficient, excessive or imbalanced consumption of nutrients leading to health problems
questions.explanation: Malnutrition is defined as the insufficient, excessive or imbalanced consumption of nutrients, which leads to health problems.

questions.question: What is stunting?
questions.explanation: Stunting is defined as low height for age. It is the result of chronic or recurrent undernutrition, usually associated with poverty, poor maternal health, and frequent illness.

questions.question: What is wasting?
questions.explanation: Wasting is defined as low weight for height. It often indicates recent and severe weight loss and usually occurs when a person has not had adequate food quality and quantity.

questions.question: What is obesity?
options: Lack of nutrients in the body
Excessive weight gain caused by imbalance between energy intake and energy released
questions.correctAnswer: Excessive weight gain caused by imbalance between energy intake and energy released
questions.explanation: Obesity is caused by an imbalance between the energy stored in the human body and the energy released. It occurs when consumption of high-energy foods increases without an equal increase in physical activity.

questions.question: What BMI value indicates obesity?
questions.explanation: A person with a BMI of 30.0 and above is classified as obese. BMI between 18.5 and 24.9 is normal weight, 25.0 to 29.9 is overweight, and below 18.5 is underweight.

questions.question: What is the BMI formula?
questions.explanation: Body mass index (BMI) = body mass (kg) / height$^2$ (metres$^2$). It was developed by Adolphe Quetelet, a Belgian statistician.

questions.question: What is substance abuse?
options: Using legal drugs only for medical purposes
Using legal or illegal drugs (substances) in the wrong way or in excess amount
questions.correctAnswer: Using legal or illegal drugs (substances) in the wrong way or in excess amount
questions.explanation: Substance abuse is using legal or illegal drugs (substances) in the wrong way or in the excess amount. Some substances like tea, coffee, and tobacco are legal but can cause serious effects when taken excessively.

questions.question: What are the three main chemical components found in cigarette smoke?
questions.explanation: The main components of cigarette or tobacco are tar (a black sticky substance), carbon monoxide (a poisonous gas), and nicotine (a stimulating and addictive compound).

questions.question: What health problem does tar in cigarette smoke cause?
questions.explanation: Tar is a black sticky substance found in cigarette that collects in the lungs. It can cause chronic bronchitis and lung cancer due to carcinogenic compounds in tar.

questions.question: How does carbon monoxide affect the body?
options: It increases oxygen levels in the blood
It combines permanently with hemoglobin, reducing oxygen transport
questions.correctAnswer: It combines permanently with hemoglobin, reducing oxygen transport
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide combines permanently with hemoglobin to form carboxyhemoglobin. This reduces the volume of oxygen carried in the blood, leading to less oxygen supplied to the heart.

questions.question: What effect does nicotine have on the body?
options: It is a stimulating and addictive compound that increases heart rate and blood pressure
questions.correctAnswer: It is a stimulating and addictive compound that increases heart rate and blood pressure
questions.explanation: Nicotine is a stimulating compound that increases heart rate and blood pressure. It activates the release of dopamine in the brain and produces addiction.

questions.question: What type of drug is alcohol classified as?
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It affects the brain by slowing down the transmission of nerve impulses, leading to loss of coordination, self-control, and slower reaction times.

questions.question: What is cirrhosis of the liver?
options: Damage to liver tissue replaced by scar tissue due to large alcohol consumption
Inflammation of the liver due to infection
questions.correctAnswer: Damage to liver tissue replaced by scar tissue due to large alcohol consumption
questions.explanation: Large amounts of alcohol damage the liver tissue, which is replaced by scar tissue, a condition known as cirrhosis. This condition may lead to death unless the person stops drinking.

questions.question: What type of drug is heroin?
questions.explanation: Heroin is a powerful depressant that slows down the nervous system. It has a chemical structure similar to endorphins and binds to endorphin receptor sites, blocking nerve transmission.

questions.question: What is the psychoactive component found in cannabis?
questions.explanation: Cannabis contains a stimulant or psychoactive component called Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC). It causes enjoyment, altered states of mind, difficulty concentrating, and reduced short-term memory.

questions.question: What is the chemical compound found in khat that affects the central nervous system?
questions.explanation: Khat contains a chemical compound known as cathinone, which affects the central nervous system (CNS). Cathinone can be found only in fresh khat leaves.

questions.question: What is the scientific name of the khat plant?
questions.explanation: Khat (Catha edulis) is a bushy plant whose leaves are chewed for their stimulant effect. It is grown in southern Arabia and Eastern Africa including Ethiopia.

questions.question: What is doping?
options: Eating a balanced diet before competition
Use of prohibited medications, drugs, or treatments in competitive sports to improve performance
questions.correctAnswer: Use of prohibited medications, drugs, or treatments in competitive sports to improve performance
questions.explanation: Doping refers to the use of prohibited medications, drugs, or treatments in competitive sports with the intention of improving athletic performance.

questions.question: Which organization tests athletes for doping?
questions.explanation: The World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) uses a battery of blood and urine tests to determine if athletes are cheating. A key tool is the biological passport program.

questions.question: What are infectious diseases?
options: Diseases caused by inherited genetic factors
Diseases caused by disease-causing organisms that can be transmitted from person to person
Diseases caused by chemical effects only
Diseases caused by poor diet only
questions.correctAnswer: Diseases caused by disease-causing organisms that can be transmitted from person to person
questions.explanation: Infectious diseases are diseases that are caused by disease-causing organisms. These types of diseases can be transmitted from person to person, such as HIV-AIDS, tuberculosis, and malaria.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a disease-causing organism?
questions.explanation: Disease-causing organisms include bacteria, viruses, protozoa, and fungi. Vitamins are nutrients, not disease-causing organisms.

questions.question: What is the causative agent of tuberculosis?
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium called Mycobacterium tuberculosis. These bacteria live inside human cells, mainly in the lungs.

questions.question: How is tuberculosis transmitted?
options: Through airborne droplets when infected people cough or sneeze
questions.correctAnswer: Through airborne droplets when infected people cough or sneeze
questions.explanation: TB bacteria enter the lungs in airborne droplets. It spreads when infected people with the active form of the illness cough or sneeze, and uninfected people inhale the droplets.

questions.question: What is the causative agent of malaria?
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by protozoa known as Plasmodium. It is transmitted by the bite of female Anopheles mosquitoes.

questions.question: What is the vector for malaria transmission?
questions.explanation: Female Anopheles mosquitoes are vectors that transmit malaria. They feed on human blood and inject Plasmodium with their saliva when feeding on a healthy person.

questions.question: What is the causative agent of HIV/AIDS?
questions.explanation: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) is caused by the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). HIV infects and destroys T-lymphocytes, weakening the immune system.

questions.question: Which type of cells does HIV infect and destroy?
questions.explanation: HIV infects and enters T-lymphocytes (also called T-helper cells), which are cells that defend our body from diseases. HIV replicates inside and destroys these cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is a mode of HIV transmission?
options: Shaking hands with an infected person
Sharing needles in intravenous drug users
Breathing the same air as an infected person
Sharing meals with an infected person
questions.correctAnswer: Sharing needles in intravenous drug users
questions.explanation: HIV can be transmitted through sharing needles, sexual intercourse, blood transfusion, mother to fetus across placenta, and mother to infant in breast milk. It is not transmitted by casual contact.

questions.question: What is the BCG vaccine used for?
questions.explanation: The BCG vaccine is the only vaccine available for TB. It is derived from animal TB bacteria and protects up to 70-80% of people who receive it. It is given during early childhood.

questions.question: What type of disease is COVID-19 caused by?
questions.explanation: COVID-19 is caused by SARS-CoV-2, a novel strain of coronavirus that first emerged in Wuhan, China in December 2019. The WHO declared it a pandemic in March 2020.

questions.question: How does the COVID-19 virus primarily spread?
options: Through droplets and virus particles released into the air when an infected person breathes, talks, coughs or sneezes
questions.correctAnswer: Through droplets and virus particles released into the air when an infected person breathes, talks, coughs or sneezes
questions.explanation: The COVID-19 virus spreads primarily through droplets and virus particles released into the air when an infected person breathes, talks, laughs, sings, coughs, or sneezes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-infectious disease?
questions.explanation: Non-infectious diseases are not caused by pathogens. They include diabetes, cancer, hypertension, asthma, sickle cell anemia, and deficiency diseases. Malaria, TB, and HIV/AIDS are infectious.

questions.question: What are non-infectious diseases caused by?
options: Malnutrition, chemical effects, inherited or genetic factors
questions.correctAnswer: Malnutrition, chemical effects, inherited or genetic factors
questions.explanation: Non-infectious diseases are caused by malnutrition, chemical effects, inherited or genetic factors, etc. They are not caused by disease-causing organisms.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a risk factor for non-infectious diseases?
questions.explanation: Tobacco use, physical inactivity, harmful use of alcohol, and unhealthy diets increase the risk of non-infectious diseases. Vaccination prevents infectious diseases.

questions.question: Who are nutritionists?
options: Researchers or scientists who study nutrition
questions.correctAnswer: Researchers or scientists who study nutrition
questions.explanation: Nutritionists are researchers or scientists who study nutrition. They study how food affects the body and provide dietary guidance for health and disease prevention.

questions.question: What is a vector in the context of infectious diseases?
options: An organism that carries a disease-causing organism and transmits it from one person to another or from an animal to a human
questions.correctAnswer: An organism that carries a disease-causing organism and transmits it from one person to another or from an animal to a human
questions.explanation: A vector is an organism that carries a disease-causing organism and transmits it from one person to another or from an animal to a human. For example, Anopheles mosquito transmits malaria.

questions.question: Which disease is caused by lack of vitamin D and results in deformed bones in children?
questions.explanation: Rickets is a deficiency disease caused by shortage of vitamin D. It results in deformed bones in the legs of children. Vitamin D can be obtained from sunlight and foods like oily fish and eggs.

questions.question: What is an endemic disease?
options: A disease occurring when a disease-causing agent exists permanently in a specific place or population
A disease that occurs suddenly in a specific area
A disease that is always fatal
questions.correctAnswer: A disease occurring when a disease-causing agent exists permanently in a specific place or population
questions.explanation: An endemic disease occurs when a disease-causing agent exists permanently in a specific place or population. For example, malaria is endemic in the Afar region of Ethiopia.

questions.question: What is a pandemic?
options: A disease limited to a small area
An epidemic that spreads far more widely throughout the whole world
A disease that only affects animals
questions.correctAnswer: An epidemic that spreads far more widely throughout the whole world
questions.explanation: A pandemic is an epidemic that spreads far more widely throughout the whole world and affects a huge number of people. An example is COVID-19.

questions.question: Which foods are good sources of vitamin C?
options: Oranges, lemons, and fresh green vegetables
questions.correctAnswer: Oranges, lemons, and fresh green vegetables
questions.explanation: Good sources of vitamin C are oranges, lemons, grapefruit, tomatoes, and fresh green vegetables. Vitamin C cannot be stored in the body, so it must be taken daily.

questions.question: Which of the following foods is a good source of calcium?
questions.explanation: Calcium is found in milk, cheese, and other dairy products. Calcium is used to build teeth and bones, make muscles contract, and help in nerve impulse transmission.

questions.question: What is the role of water in the human body?
options: Acts as a solvent and transport medium for substances throughout the body
questions.correctAnswer: Acts as a solvent and transport medium for substances throughout the body
questions.explanation: Body fluids such as blood, lymph and tissue fluid are mainly composed of water. Water acts as a solvent and as a transport medium for substances throughout the body.

questions.question: What is the main function of vitamin D in the human body?
options: Helps in the absorption of calcium and phosphorus to build bone and teeth
questions.correctAnswer: Helps in the absorption of calcium and phosphorus to build bone and teeth
questions.explanation: Vitamin D helps in the absorption of calcium and phosphorus through the gut wall, which is important to build bone and teeth. It is the only vitamin the body can make from sunlight.
